message.content:
# Four Positions on Open-Source AI Restrictions

---

## 1. Completely Open (No Restrictions)

**Steelman:**
The strongest case for unrestricted open-source AI rests on three pillars. First, **security through transparency**: closed systems have repeatedly failed (data breaches, backdoors, vendor lock-in), while open systems benefit from collective scrutiny—thousands of developers examining code catch vulnerabilities that no single corporation would reveal. Second, **democratization prevents tyranny**: concentrated AI power in a handful of tech giants or governments is far more dangerous than distributed access. The printing press didn't cause the Reformation's wars because of openness—it was the *suppression* of printing by authorities that created the worst conflicts. Third, **the capability genie is irreversibly out of the bottle**: compute is cheapening, knowledge is proliferating, and restrictions will only prevent good actors from accessing safety measures while bad actors ignore them anyway.

**Typical Counter-Argument:**
Existential and catastrophic risks from open-source AI—bioterror, AI-driven cyberattacks, autonomous weapons, sophisticated disinformation at population scale—cannot be adequately addressed through transparency alone.
